title: Gravity without a loop
summary: Three bodies chasing each other round a figure-eight, with no loop over pairs: every pair's displacement is one table, every pull one expression, every acceleration one reduce. Ends on the live page.

scenes.heading: Gravity, without a loop
scenes.narration: Three bodies, pulling on each other. No loop over pairs.
lines: Every pair of bodies at once, as arrays.

scenes.heading: 1. Every pair, one table
scenes.narration: First, how far apart is every pair? Subtract every x from every x. That is one table. The same for y. Stack the two, and you have a cube.

lines.xtl: (u:p_lane x '- t_able x) c_at u:p_lane y '- t_able y

lines: Every x minus every x: a table. The same for y.
Stack them: a cube of every pair's displacement.

scenes.heading: 2. Every pair's pull
scenes.narration: Gravity is an inverse square. One expression gives the pull between every pair at once.
lines: The inverse square law, for all pairs at once.

scenes.heading: 3. One reduce
scenes.narration: Now add up each row. One reduce turns every pair's pull into each body's acceleration.

lines.xtl: n_eg '+ r_/_3 d * (2 c_at s_hape w) r_eshape w

lines: Sum over the second body: each body's acceleration.

boards.label: accelerations: a column a body, x above y

scenes.heading: 4. Step, and repeat
scenes.narration: Kick, drift, kick. Repeat the step, and three bodies chase each other around a figure eight.
lines: Kick, drift, kick. Three equal masses, one figure-eight.
